method: Exhaustive filesystem sweep of the research worktree for jpg/jpeg/png/heic/webp, excluding node_modules, .git, android/ and ios/ build trees. Every candidate was opened and visually reviewed. No image was admitted on the basis of its filename or its registration as a fixture.

headline.verdict: BLOCKED — the 75-case first-baseline dataset cannot be assembled from accessible approved imagery. No case was fabricated to close the gap.

criticalFindings.title: Phase 0A classed all 8 fixtures 'approved' from their existence as QA fixtures, not from an authorization record.
criticalFindings.detail: fixtures-inventory v0.1.0 recorded authorizationStatus 'approved_qa_fixture' for all 8 with the justification 'DEV-only QA fixture registered in constants/qaFixtures.js'. Registration as a QA fixture is not a license, a model release, or a use authorization. No licence file, provenance record, purchase record or model release exists in the repository for any of the 8 images.
criticalFindings.consequence: Every one of the 8 currently carries an unverified authorization claim. Section 5 explicitly warns against assuming a file is approved merely because it exists.

criticalFindings.title: assets/qa_fixtures/bottom_skirt.jpg is excluded from the evaluation dataset pending provenance.
observableFacts: One identifiable person is the subject, face unobscured and in focus.
The setting is an interior residential stairwell with identifying detail, including a wall marking that reads as a unit number.
Framing, lighting and composition are those of a casual personal photograph rather than a studio or catalogue shoot; the other apparel fixtures in the directory are visibly commercial imagery.
The file carries a Photoshop APP13 metadata block, no EXIF GPS, and no camera Make/Model.
unknowns: model release or any record of the subject's permission
capture date, photographer, or how the file was obtained
the subject's age, and any basis on which to estimate it
criticalFindings.evidentiaryNote: Age, legal status and absence of permission are NOT asserted. None has been independently verified. The basis for exclusion is undocumented provenance combined with an identifiable person in a private setting — not a conclusion about the subject.
criticalFindings.consequence: Excluded from the governed dataset (privacyDisposition blocked_private) pending provenance. Masking would address identifiability but not the provenance gap, which is why it is excluded rather than remediated.
criticalFindings.escalation: Full report at docs/scanner-accuracy/phase0c-fixture-escalation.md. Empirically confirmed to have shipped in a production Expo export dated 2026-07-13 (all 8 fixture md5s present). The __DEV__ gate was added 2026-07-28 and has NOT reached origin/master or release/ios-v18-build-prep.

criticalFindings.title: 3 of 8 fixtures contain human faces and had no face review before Phase 0B.
criticalFindings.detail: top.jpg (fully identifiable frontal face), dress.jpg (identifiable model face), outerwear.jpg (partial face: jaw, mouth, chin). All three were recorded in v0.1.0 as privacyDisposition 'governed_fixture_reference' with no faceReviewState field at all.
criticalFindings.consequence: Each requires an approved masked derivative before admission. They are not admissible as-is.

criticalFindings.title: 2 of 8 fixtures retain EXIF, XMP and Photoshop metadata.
criticalFindings.detail: bottom_jeans.jpg carries an EXIF APP1 (IFD0 tags 0x112 orientation, 0x11a/0x11b/0x128 resolution, 0x131 Software, 0x132 DateTime, 0x8769 ExifIFD pointer), an XMP APP1, and a 5632-byte Photoshop APP13 block. dress.jpg carries EXIF (0x131 Software, 0x8769 ExifIFD) and a Photoshop APP13 block. Verified by direct JPEG segment parsing.
criticalFindings.gpsFinding: NO GPS IFD is present in either file. An initial byte-pattern scan appeared to show a GPS tag in dress.jpg; parsing the actual IFD structure disproved it. No camera Make/Model tag (0x010F/0x0110) is present in either IFD0.
criticalFindings.consequence: EXIF stripping is required before admission but the privacy exposure is low: no location and no camera identity.

criticalFindings.title: accessory.jpg is a multi-item scene mislabelled as a single accessory case.
criticalFindings.detail: The image contains a striped shoulder bag, a pair of aviator sunglasses, and a hardcover book, on a dock. v0.1.0 labels it category 'accessories', clothingType 'unknown'. Production would be expected to return status multiple_items_need_selection for this frame.
criticalFindings.consequence: It is a legitimate multi-item DETECTION case and a poor single-item identification case. Scoring it as a single accessory would penalise correct behaviour.

criticalFindings.title: top.jpg carries a non-verifiable brand-like mark.
criticalFindings.detail: The hoodie bears a printed 'COQ' wordmark with a device above it. This is characteristic of a commercial garment mock-up template rather than a real retail brand. It cannot be verified against any product record.
criticalFindings.consequence: Brand ground truth must remain not_visible/unknown. The image is however a genuine candidate for the 'misleading brand-like design' stratum, where the correct model behaviour is to decline rather than name a brand.

sources.authorizationReference: constants/qaFixtures.js registration only — NOT a licence or model release. See INV-1.
sources.existingLabels: category only, from fixture id intent. All finer fields recorded as 'unknown' in dataset v0.1.0.
sources.facePresence: 3 of 8 (top, dress, outerwear); 1 further case (bottom_skirt) excluded pending provenance, see INV-2
sources.exifStatus: 2 of 8 retain EXIF/XMP/Photoshop metadata; 0 of 8 carry GPS; 0 of 8 carry camera Make/Model
sources.permittedUse: PENDING — internal evaluation by governed reference and hash only, contingent on the owner resolving INV-1.

sources.exclusionReason: These are synthetic placeholder blobs, not photographs. Six are byte-identical 450-byte JPEG stubs; screenshot.png is 70 bytes; both .heic files are ASCII text beginning 'heic-fixture-pla'. The README states they are 'Synthetic non-personal fixtures for deterministic unit/integration harnesses'. multi-item-outfit.jpg contains no outfit. They carry zero visual ground truth.

Line-art UI tiles on a dark background, each captioned 'K-SCAN DEMO CATALOG'. They are schematic garment outlines, not photographs. They carry no material, no brand, no exact product and no real-world colour. Scoring against them would measure the model's response to an icon, not to a garment.

Tight head-and-shoulders avatar portraits. No scannable garment is present — at most a sliver of collar. Excluded on relevance (no garment subject) and on privacy posture (face-dominant imagery has no place in an evaluation corpus transmitted to a model provider).
App icons, splash art and marketing hero images. Not garment photographs.

sources.permittedUse: Text-proxy regression only. NOT visual ground truth and never admissible to a visual accuracy baseline.
Deterministic quality-tune regression only. Not a statistical accuracy study.

sources.authorizationReference: fixtures-inventory v0.1.0 blockedPendingAuthorization: 'Not approved for Build 4 evaluation export or commit.'
sources.permittedUse: NONE. Not accessed during Phase 0B. Exporting real user scan imagery into an evaluation corpus requires an explicit owner authorization and a lawful basis that does not exist today.
sources.note: Deliberately not queried. This phase is offline and non-production; enumerating user imagery would itself be a production data access.

sources.authorizationReference: fixtures-inventory v0.1.0: 'Correction-event schema may be designed; live import not authorized.'

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A person's lower legs walking on wet sand at sunset, wearing one visible red low-top lace-up sneaker; the other foot is bare.
perFixtureDisposition.labelableFields: category=footwear, clothingType=sneaker, subtype=low_top_sneaker, primaryColor=red, brand=not_visible, exactProduct=unknown

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A white ceramic mug bearing a printed 'White Sands Missile Range' emblem, on a wooden table.
perFixtureDisposition.privateBackgroundRisk: low — indoor table surface, no identifying detail
perFixtureDisposition.labelableFields: all fashion fields = not_applicable; expectedResultType=insufficient_evidence; expectedAbstention=true

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A commercial product photo of a model from the neck down, wearing mid-blue straight-leg faded denim jeans, a white t-shirt, and white low-top canvas sneakers, on a grey studio backdrop.
perFixtureDisposition.exifDetail: EXIF IFD0 (Software, DateTime), XMP, 5632-byte Photoshop APP13. No GPS. No camera Make/Model.
perFixtureDisposition.labelableFields: category=pants, clothingType=jeans, subtype=straight_jeans, primaryColor=blue, material=denim, brand=not_visible

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A blue-and-white striped canvas shoulder bag with black leather straps, a pair of gold-framed brown-lens aviator sunglasses, and a hardcover book, arranged on a wooden dock beside water.
perFixtureDisposition.labelableFields: MULTI-ITEM. Correct expected behaviour is multiple_items_need_selection, not a single accessory identification. Requires selected-item labels per candidate.

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A commercial garment mock-up: a man facing the camera wearing a plain white pullover hoodie with a printed 'COQ' wordmark, over dark jeans, on a white background.
perFixtureDisposition.derivativeReason: Fully identifiable frontal face. A masked or cropped derivative must be produced and approved before admission.
perFixtureDisposition.labelableFields: category=top, clothingType=hoodie, subtype=pullover_hoodie, primaryColor=white, brand=not_visible (see INV-6)

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A bridal catalogue photo: a model in a white strapless A-line floor-length gown with a champagne sash, against dark wood panelling.
perFixtureDisposition.exifDetail: EXIF IFD0 (Software), Photoshop APP13. No GPS. No camera Make/Model.
perFixtureDisposition.derivativeReason: Identifiable model face; EXIF strip also required.

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: A black-and-white fashion photo, cropped close: a distressed leather biker-style jacket with a ribbed knit inner collar and zip detail, worn by a person whose jaw, mouth and chin are visible but whose eyes are cropped out.
perFixtureDisposition.derivativeReason: Partial but recognisable facial features. Owner review required to decide mask vs admit.
perFixtureDisposition.labelableFields: category=outerwear, clothingType=jacket, subtype=moto_jacket, primaryColor=NOT LABELABLE (greyscale image — colour ground truth is unrecoverable), material=leather
perFixtureDisposition.colourCaveat: This image is monochrome. primaryColor must be labelled not_visible. Scoring the model's colour output against any concrete colour would be measuring a fabrication on our side, not theirs.

perFixtureDisposition.visualContent: An identifiable person photographed in an interior residential stairwell. Composition is that of a casual personal photograph rather than commercial product imagery.
perFixtureDisposition.exclusionReason: Undocumented provenance combined with an identifiable person in a private setting. No source, licence, model release or capture record exists. Masking would address identifiability but not the provenance gap, so a derivative does not resolve it. Age and absence of permission are NOT asserted — neither has been verified. See INV-2.
blockedBy: INV-2 EXCLUDED pending provenance — owner escalation required

coverageGapAgainstTarget.note: Measured against the section 6 first-baseline targets. 'Have' counts only images that are admissible or admissible-after-masking, and excludes the rejected fixture. It does NOT assume INV-1 is resolved.

bags.caveat: the one bag is inside a multi-item frame

eyewear.caveat: same multi-item frame as the bag

multiImageSameItemSets.caveat: NO same-item multi-angle set exists in any accessible source

exactProductKnowable.caveat: NO accessible image has a verifiable SKU, product page or purchase record. Exact-product ground truth cannot be established for any of them.

hardestGaps: multi-image same-item sets: 0 of 10. Section 4.10 scoring is implemented and tested, but there is nothing to run it on.
exact-product-knowable: 0 of 10. Compounded by measurement ceiling MC-1, which makes the stratum unmeasurable on the deployed path even if the imagery existed.
mirror photographs, screenshots, store displays: 0 of 13 combined. No accessible source contains any.

rejected.reason: INV-2 — undocumented provenance with an identifiable person in a private setting. Age and permission are not asserted.
